title: The King, the Holy, praised by all things.
subtitle: Four names before the Friday surah begins
then: The Prophet ﷺ used to recite this surah in the Friday prayer. Ibn Kathir says it opens by telling us that {idea}everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Allah{/idea}, living creatures and lifeless things alike. He is the King in full control, and the Holy, free of every shortcoming.
now: Friday morning. You are rushing: work, the school run, a meeting before the prayer. Pause for one breath. {idea}The room you are in, the chair, the window, the light, are already praising the King.{/idea} You are the one who can choose to.
old: Worship is something only people do, and only at certain times.
new: All of creation is praising its King, and I get to join with words.
try: This Friday, before the prayer, say SubhanAllah ten times slowly, thinking of the King and the Holy.

title: A messenger from among them, reciting, purifying, teaching.
subtitle: What the Prophet ﷺ was sent to do
then: Ibn Kathir says the Arabs had once followed the religion of Ibrahim, then changed it for idol worship and doubt. This verse is the answer to Ibrahim's old prayer for a messenger from among them. {idea}He recited, purified, and taught the Book and wisdom{/idea}, to people who {trap}had been in clear error{/trap}.
now: You watch hours of Islamic clips. You know a lot. But is anything being cleaned out of you, the temper, the envy, the habit? {idea}Recite, purify, teach.{/idea} Knowledge alone was never the whole of it.
old: Learning more facts about Islam is what makes me a better Muslim.
new: The Quran came to clean my heart, not just to fill my head.
try: After your next Quran reading, ask: what one thing in me does this verse want to clean?

title: And others who have not yet joined them.
subtitle: The message was always meant to reach you
then: Abu Hurayrah said they were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when this was revealed. They asked three times who these others were. He put his hand on Salman al-Farisi and said: {reward}if faith were at the Pleiades, men from these people would reach it{/reward}. Mujahid said it means all later non-Arabs who believe.
now: You were born centuries later, in a city the Companions never heard of, maybe into a family that never practised. {reward}You are part of "others who have not yet joined them".{/reward} {idea}You were expected.{/idea}
old: The real Muslims were the first ones. I am just a distant copy.
new: Allah named people like me in His Book before I was born.
try: Make a dua today for the Companions, and thank Allah that the message reached you.

title: That is Allah's favor, given to whom He wills.
subtitle: Guidance is a gift, not a reward we earned first
then: After naming the first believers and those who would join later, the passage says this is {reward}the favor of Allah{/reward}, and He is the Owner of mighty favor. Ibn Kathir says the Messenger ﷺ came when the way had become obscure, at the time it was most needed.
now: It is easy to feel proud of being the one in the family who prays, or the one who "came back". {idea}Every step of that was a gift.{/idea} {trap}Pride turns a gift into a trophy.{/trap}
old: I am guided because I made better choices than others.
new: My guidance is Allah's favor to me, and He can give it to anyone.
try: Think of someone you look down on for their faith. Make a sincere dua for them instead.

title: Like a donkey carrying a load of books.
subtitle: Carrying scripture without carrying it out
then: The verse speaks of those given the Torah who did not carry out what it said. Ibn Kathir explains that a donkey carrying books uses only its strength. {trap}They read the letters but did not act on the meanings{/trap}, and unlike the donkey, they had minds that could have understood.
now: A beautiful Quran on the shelf. Apps with every tafsir. Verses memorised as a child. {trap}And none of it touches how you speak to your mother or spend your salary.{/trap} {idea}The question is not what you carry, but what carries you.{/idea}
old: Having the Quran close and reciting it is enough.
new: A book on my back is weight. A book in my life is guidance.
try: Choose one verse you already know by heart and do one thing today that it asks.

title: If you are Allah's chosen, then wish for death.
subtitle: A challenge to a claim of special closeness
then: Some among the Jews of Madinah claimed they alone were Allah's friends. Ibn Kathir says the challenge meant: {idea}if you are sure you are right, call on Allah to let the misguided side die{/idea}. The same challenge appears in Surah Al-Baqarah.
now: It is easy to say "we are the good ones", our family, our mosque, our circle. {trap}Then picture meeting Allah tonight.{/trap} {idea}If that thought frightens you, the confidence was a label, not a reality.{/idea} The verse asks you, not just them.
old: I belong to the right group, so I am safe with Allah.
new: Closeness to Allah shows in being ready to meet Him, not in a label.
try: Ask yourself honestly: if I met Allah tonight, what is the one thing I would want to fix first? Start on it.

title: They never wish for it, because of what they sent ahead.
subtitle: Deeds go before us and wait
then: Allah says they will never wish for death {trap}because of what their hands have sent before them{/trap}. Ibn Kathir names it: disbelief, injustice and sins. And {idea}Allah knows the wrongdoers{/idea} well.
now: You flinch at a funeral, at a hospital corridor, at a scary scan result. Part of it is natural. But part of it is the list in your head of things you have not put right. {idea}You can still send different things ahead.{/idea}
old: I fear death because it is scary and unknown.
new: What makes death heavy is what I have sent ahead, and I can still change that.
try: Send one good thing ahead today: a secret charity, an apology, or a prayer no one sees.

title: The death you run from will meet you.
subtitle: Running away only changes the direction you face
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to say that the death they flee {trap}will surely meet them{/trap}, and then they return to the Knower of the unseen and the seen. Ibn Kathir links it to another verse: death overtakes you even in high, strong towers.
now: You avoid writing a will. You change the subject when someone mentions the grave. You keep busy. {trap}None of it slows death down.{/trap} {idea}Facing it calmly is what changes how you live today.{/idea}
old: If I do not think about death, I can live more freely.
new: Death is coming toward me anyway, so I want to meet it ready.
try: Spend two quiet minutes today thinking about your own death, then do one thing you would want done before it.

title: When Friday's call comes, go and leave the trade.
subtitle: A weekly pause that is better for you
then: Ibn Kathir says Jumu'ah comes from gathering, the day believers meet each week. Al-Hasan said that hastening here {idea}is not done with the feet, but with the heart, the intention and humility{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ told people to come to prayer with calm and dignity.
now: It is Friday, 12:40. Your inbox is full and a client call is booked. The adhan app buzzes. {trap}Five more minutes, just this one email.{/trap} {idea}Close the laptop. The pause is the gift.{/idea}
old: Friday prayer interrupts my busiest part of the day.
new: The weekly pause for Allah is better for me than the business I leave.
try: This Friday, set an alarm fifteen minutes before Jumu'ah and stop work when it rings.

title: Then go out, seek His bounty, and remember Him often.
subtitle: Work is welcome once worship has its place
then: Right after telling believers to leave trade for the prayer, Allah tells them to {reward}go out and seek His bounty{/reward} once it is done. Work was never the enemy. The verse only asks them to {idea}keep remembering Allah much{/idea} while they do it.
now: You walk out of the mosque and straight back to the warehouse, the clinic, the shop. {idea}The remembering does not stop at the door.{/idea} A quiet bismillah before a meeting, alhamdulillah when a sale goes through.
old: Once prayer is over, I am back in the real world.
new: Earning a living is seeking Allah's bounty, and remembering Him can come with me.
try: Pick one moment at work today, like opening your laptop, and attach a short dhikr to it.

title: They ran to the caravan and left you standing.
subtitle: When something shiny walks past during the sermon
then: Jabir said a caravan reached Madinah while the Prophet ﷺ was giving the Friday sermon. {trap}People left, and only twelve men remained.{/trap} This verse came down. Allah answered: {reward}what is with Him is better{/reward}, and He is the best of providers.
now: The imam is speaking and your phone lights up: a sale, a match score, a message. Your attention runs out the door. {idea}The caravan still arrives every Friday.{/idea} {reward}Be one of the ones who stay.{/reward}
old: If I miss this deal or this moment, I lose out.
new: What is with Allah is better, and He is the One who provides anyway.
try: At your next Jumu'ah or class, switch your phone fully off before it starts.
